subject: Humanities
focus: Plan a respectful memorial layout privately using checked facts, an original dedication and symbol, and a safe line on responsibility today.
enquiry: How can a memorial design show respect and accurate learning?

source_workbook.basis: Owner brief: LAUNCH Weekly Spring row 44. Workbook not re-read; inherited workbook provenance is retained for traceability only.

assessment_generic: Formative memorial-design planning with respect, accuracy and reasons. Assess the plan and its choices, not grief, artistic skill or a public performance. This is not evidence of publishing, software operation or accredited completion.

Supported: Use the blank layout guide. Plan one part at a time. An adult may read the cards exactly; choose three facts from F1–F4/F6.
Keep each fact’s code. Use the frame for your own dedication and responsibility line. Describe your own symbol idea in words if sketching is unhelpful.
Use the checklist with an adult. Keep all parts, one change and your reason. Point, type or direct a scribe while keeping your own ideas.
Independent: Plan your own layout with all required parts. Use three distinct facts from F1–F4/F6 in your own short wording, with codes.
Write your dedication and a safe responsibility line. Design your own simple symbol; explain what it means and why it fits.
Check tone, accuracy and dignity. Make one reasoned change. Keep the plan private on paper or in a plain offline document.
Aspire: Keep the same common finish. Explain how the order of your title, dedication, facts and symbol helps a reader learn with care.
Explain a limit: one design cannot tell every life or the whole history. Do not use a stronger emotional effect as a measure of respect.
Revise a choice that could mislead or reduce dignity. Explain why your version is more accurate or respectful, without adding images, accounts or publication.

sensitive_response_route: Point to PAUSE or tell the adult quietly. Use the agreed supervised place. You do not need to explain to the group. When ready, choose a private recap or more time with the quiet task. The adult will help you rejoin.
quiet_alternative: Quiet task: put these made-up daily times in order: 14:00 club; 08:30 reading; 12:00 lunch; 10:00 break. Copy or point to the first and last. Then sort pencil and book, cup and plate, by use. No history words or personal story are needed.
staff_care_rules: The supplied text completes this private planning lesson. Add no imagery or survivor testimony in any form: no quotation, paraphrase, invented voice, composite, audio, video or live browsing. No individual victim’s name, real photograph or website address is supplied or used. Do not introduce an extra story or archive item. The school’s chosen memorial-day resource may be reviewed privately by the teacher only if school-approved and within the care limits; no title, organisation or address is named.

Keep the dignity and full lives of people in view. Do not use imagine-you-are tasks, victim roles, historical role play, comparisons of suffering or personal family-history questions. Do not ask any learner to speak for Jewish people, survivors or a whole community. Do not invent a life story to make the topic feel personal.

Participation is thoughtful learning, not a performance of grief. Do not require a particular feeling, silence, prayer, pledge, public statement, personal disclosure or completed dedication read aloud. Quiet work, pointing, private response and passing are allowed. Assess the design choices, accuracy and care, not visible sadness or artistic skill.

Agree a discreet PAUSE signal, supervising adult, quiet place and private return check before teaching. Keep both learners supervised. If a sole adult cannot supervise separate spaces, use a calm place in the room or pause the whole group while seeking usual support. Never send a learner away alone.

For distress, stop the demand, acknowledge it calmly and offer the agreed route without sanction or a public explanation. Do not probe or insist on a history recap while the learner is upset. Follow the school’s existing safeguarding arrangements for disclosures and use the appropriate private record.

Interrupt antisemitism calmly and firmly. Name the harm without repeating a slur. Hostility towards Jewish people is unacceptable. Correct a falsehood briefly and follow school procedures. Do not debate Holocaust denial or require learners to defend victims’ rights. Victims were not responsible for their persecution.

For flippancy or laughter, stop and reset respectful listening. A nervous response is possible, but harm still needs addressing. Follow up privately, check those affected and use existing procedures for targeted, repeated or serious incidents. Avoid shaming or guessing motives.

A warning is a reason to learn and act carefully, not a prediction that every unfair act leads to genocide. Do not equate everyday disagreement with the Holocaust. Remembrance alone cannot prevent hatred; education, laws, institutions and human choices matter too. Learners do not carry personal responsibility for preventing genocide.

Offer the neutral quiet task and a private readiness check. It is not evidence of the memorial-design outcome. Record deferred work honestly and offer a later supported return. A partner’s design or a copied adult model does not establish the learner’s understanding.

This is a plan, not a live digital product. Work remains on paper or in a plain offline document. Do not create accounts, search for pictures, use online design tools, publish, share, export or upload work, including to an evidence app. Record work location offline; leave E unmarked. The learner may describe an original simple symbol in words or sketch their own idea privately. Supply no image or finished symbol to copy. A symbol’s meaning must be explained as this learner’s design choice, not a claim about a whole community.
context: A memorial can help people remember and learn. Today you plan a digital memorial as a private storyboard on paper or in a plain offline document. You will not build a website. The plan keeps people’s dignity, accurate history and safe responsibility in view. Nothing is published, shared or uploaded.

hinge.question: Which plan fits this lesson? A: Copy a real photo and put the design online. B: Use three checked facts, your own dedication and symbol idea, and keep the plan private. C: Invent a survivor’s voice to make the design moving.
hinge.answer_and_decision_rule: B, with a reason from tone, accuracy or dignity. A breaks the photo and privacy rules. C invents an account and takes someone else’s voice. If needed, model a fact plus code and a private planning choice, then use the parallel check before independent work.
hinge.parallel: A design uses calm words but includes a made-up sentence spoken by a victim. Is it ready? No. Remove the invented voice. Use a checked fact and the learner’s own dedication, without an individual victim name.

pair_work: Design Planner points to a part of the blank layout; Respect Checker asks how tone, accuracy or dignity will be kept. Swap roles. A learner may instead check a generic choice privately with the adult, without sharing their dedication or design. Keep each learner’s own work.
